messages:
maya: Quick sync — after yesterday's Europe GPU saturation, I'm proposing we move from hard-rejects for best-effort traffic to an SLO-aware soft-queue + graceful degrade pattern. Thoughts?

devon: curious for the perf tradeoffs. Soft-queue how long are we talking? we already saw tail latency jumps.

maya: thinking about per-customer queue_budget + token-priority. baseline soft-queue window 150ms, spike-bound 800ms for low-tier, then degrade to quantized model (faster, lower quality) before rejecting.

ricardo: huge improvement for PLG users if we don't just drop. But operationally we need to ensure KV cache pressure doesn't explode with long queues. do we have metrics to cap queued KV size?

maya: good call. plan includes queue size cap and KV cache backpressure metric exposed to ops. if kv_backpressure > 0.7 then we accelerate degrade path.

eve: can we make this region-aware? EU had node-level saturation but US was fine. we should prefer cross-region warm-fallbacks before degrading.

devon: +1 for region-aware routing. fallback order: same-region warm instance -> compatible model smaller sequence -> degraded quantized model -> reject. Need to define cost delta for each step.

maya: proposing fallback penalties so billing/accounting knows cost of each step. also want a per-SLA opt-out: enterprise customers can pin to no-degrade mode (reject-only) with reserved capacity. smaller customers get queue/degrade.

ricardo: operational checklist: feature flag gating, canary on 10% traffic EU region, expose metrics: queued_count, avg_queue_ms, degrade_rate, reject_rate, kv_backpressure. also add a runtime kill switch.

infra-bot: deployment plan created: feature-flag sla-aware-queue -> canary=eu-10pct, rollout windows [01:00-05:00 UTC]. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/4123 :white_check_mark:

maya: sample policy snippet I sketched (for config):

```json
{
  "policy_name": "sla-aware-queue-v1",
  "soft_queue_ms": 150,
  "max_queue_ms_per_customer": 8000,
  "degrade_order": ["small-seq-model-v2-q8", "cpu-fallback"],
  "kv_backpressure_threshold": 0.7,
  "region_fallback_priority": ["same-region-warm", "neighbor-region-warm"],
  "exceptions": {"enterprise": "no-degrade-reserved"}
}
```

eve: two ask items: 1) how do we score requests so we don't let a single noisy tenant hog the soft queue? 2) what's the expected cost delta when we warm neighbor region?

maya: 1) we use a per-tenant token budget that refills per-second + priority buckets (interactive vs batch). 2) cost delta estimate: warm neighbor region ~ +12% per-request; quantized degrade path ~ -35% per-token cost but quality drop needs eval. I'll add numbers to the PR.

devon: can we run a simulated replay on last week's spike to estimate degrade_rate and user-visible latency impact before canary?

ricardo: I can run the replay against the simulator tomorrow. will output expected metrics and edge cases (KV eviction churn, long-tail queue starvation).

maya: thanks. next steps: ricardo to run sim, dev to add cost model to PR, eve to verify region routing heuristics, I'll own rollout and telemetry. canary target tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

sre-oncall: make sure runbooks updated for new failure modes (stuck queues, high kv_backpressure). add pager thresholds for degrade_rate > 10% and queue_ms p50 > 300ms.

maya: noted. will update runbook and link it in PR. :thumbsup:
